question.text: What does 'open interest' represent in the context of exchange-traded interest rate futures?

answer.text: The total number of outstanding contracts (counted from one side only) at any point in time
The total number of buy and sell contracts combined
The total number of contracts traded during the day
The number of unique participants with open positions

explanation.text: The Logic: Open interest is the total number of futures or options contracts that are outstanding (not closed) in a trading cycle. Because every long has a matching short, only one side is counted - 100 outstanding contracts means OI = 100, not 200. The Trap: Combining both sides double-counts. Daily traded volume is a flow measure; open interest is a stock of unsettled contracts and changes only as positions are created or closed. Note: The workbook's OI / price table reads as: rising underlying with rising OI is long buildup (bullish); rising underlying with falling OI is end of bullish trend; falling underlying with rising OI is short buildup (bearish); falling underlying with falling OI is end of bearish trend.
